entries.proposition: 🔴 THE ROLES ARE THE OPPOSITE OF WHAT THE STATE ATTRIBUTES TO THIS PAPER. Here WWOX is not ITCH's substrate: it is ITCH's ANTAGONIST, and the protein stabilised is ΔNp63α. A commit candidate in this repository cites this paper for 'direct ITCH/proteasomal stabilization', which reads a result about WWOX blocking ITCH from degrading a third protein as though it were about ITCH stabilising WWOX. Substrate, stabiliser and direction are all inverted.
entries.snippet: Altogether, these results suggest that WWOX antagonizes ITCH effect on ΔNp63α and stabilizes its protein levels

entries.proposition: WHOSE SUBSTRATE ITCH ACTUALLY IS, IN THIS PAPER. The premise the whole study builds on: ITCH ubiquitinates and degrades ΔNp63α. WWOX enters as the competitor for that interaction, never as the target of it.
entries.snippet: ΔNp63α ubiquitination and degradation is mediated by the ubiquitin E3-ligase ITCH

entries.proposition: 🔴 AND THE AUTHORS' OWN WORD FOR THE RELATIONSHIP IS 'COMPETES'. Not ubiquitinates, not stabilises — competes. This is the Discussion stating the mechanism in one sentence.
entries.snippet: we show that WWOX competes with ITCH on binding to ΔNp63α and inhibits ΔNp63α ubiquitination mediated by ITCH and thus increases ΔNp63α protein stability
entries.anchor: Discussion, the paragraph on WW-domain competition
entries.found_or_sought: sought — I went to the Discussion for the authors' own summary once the Results had already inverted the roles

entries.proposition: 🔴 WHERE THE WORD 'PROTEASOMAL' IN OUR ATTRIBUTION COMES FROM, AND WHOSE PROTEASOME IT IS. The proteasome in this paper degrades ΔNp63α, and WWOX blocks that degradation. So our phrase 'direct ITCH/proteasomal stabilization' borrows a real word from a real sentence and reattaches it to the wrong protein. AND IT SETTLES THE QUESTION FT-062 WAS WRITTEN TO ASK: the two words do not belong to the same mechanism. PMID 24550385 and PMID 26675548 both say K63-linked and degradation-INDEPENDENT for ITCH acting on WWOX; this paper says proteasomal for ITCH acting on ΔNp63α. Two different substrates, two different chain types, two different outcomes.
entries.snippet: To further show that WWOX stabilizes ΔNp63α by specifically inhibiting its degradation via the proteasome
entries.anchor: Results, the MG132 experiment; the panel is Figure 3f
entries.found_or_sought: sought — FT-062 asked which of the two words this paper uses, and this is the sentence that carries it

entries.proposition: 🔴 AND THE MEASURED ABSENCES, WHICH ARE WHAT MAKE THE INVERSION CERTAIN RATHER THAN LIKELY. Across the whole body: 'K63' occurs ZERO times, 'Lys-63' ZERO times, and there is no sentence anywhere describing WWOX as ubiquitinated — zero hits for 'ubiquitination of WWOX' or 'WWOX ubiquitination'. The K63 chemistry that DL-THER-095 rests on is simply not in this paper. What is here is 26 mentions of ITCH, 8 of stabilization and 6 of proteasome, and every one of them is about ΔNp63α. A negative measured on several independent probes that agree is stronger than a positive on one.

entries.proposition: THE FRAME THAT RECONCILES THIS PAPER WITH PMID 24550385, AND IT IS THE AUTHORS' OWN. WWOX both IS a substrate of ITCH (K63, stabilising, PMID 24550385) and COMPETES with ITCH for its other substrates (here, and for ErbB4 and p73). Both can hold, because both run through WW1 and PY motifs. INFERENZA WITH A THERAPEUTIC EDGE: raising ITCH activity to stabilise WWOX would simultaneously increase ITCH-mediated degradation of its other targets — ΔNp63α here, p73 in Figure 7 of PMID 24550385. An ITCH lever is not selective for WWOX, and neither paper says so alone.
entries.snippet: WWOX can compete with other WW domain-containing proteins, like YAP and ITCH, for binding common target proteins, such as ErbB4 and p73
entries.found_or_sought: sought — I looked for whether the authors themselves reconcile the two roles, and they do

entries.proposition: THE PANEL BEHIND THE CENTRAL CLAIM, INSPECTED AND CONSISTENT. Figure 3 carries the whole mechanism and supports it: ITCH increases the ΔNp63α ubiquitin ladder and adding WWOX collapses it; cycloheximide chase shows ΔNp63α maintained with WWOX and decaying with the non-binding Y33R mutant; WWOX knockdown lowers endogenous ΔNp63α. Nothing here contradicts the text. What the panel confirms is precisely the relationship our attribution inverts.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 3, panels a-f. Panel a: three lanes with WWOX -/-/+, Flag-ITCH -/+/+, Myc-ΔNp63α +/+/+, HA-Ub +/+/+; the anti-HA ubiquitin smear is moderate in lane 1, strongest in lane 2 and visibly reduced in lane 3, with rows below for HA-ΔNp63, Flag-ITCH and WWOX. Panel c: CHX 0/3/6 h for HA-ΔNp63 alone, with Myc-WWOX, and with Myc-WWOX-Y33R, over rows HA-ΔNp63, Myc-WWOX and GAPDH; the ΔNp63 band falls sharply in the first and third groups and is maintained in the WWOX group. Panel d: CHX 0/4/8 h for Control, Ad-GFP, Ad-WWOX and Ad-WWOX-Y33R with rows ΔNp63α, WWOX and Vinculin. Panel e: two lanes EV and KD with rows ΔNp63α, WWOX and GAPDH, both bands lower in KD. Panel f: SaOS-2 ΔNp63 with a construct table and MG132, rows ΔNp63α, WWOX and Vinculin.

entries.proposition: 🔴 A FRACTIONATION CONTROL DESCRIBED AS EXCLUSIVE WHEN THE PANEL SHOWS IT IS NOT. The word carries weight here because the paper's sequestration claim depends on where ΔNp63α is, and a leaky fraction is exactly what would produce an apparent shift. The direction of the reported shift is visible in the panel and is not in question; the description of the control is.

The WWOX row is blank throughout the nuclear fraction, consistent with the paper's own description of WWOX as predominantly cytoplasmic, and the ΔNp63α shift the text reports is visible.

In the nuclear block ΔNp63α is strong in two lanes, the WWOX row is blank, Lamin is strong and GAPDH IS VISIBLE IN ALL THREE LANES.

entries.proposition: 🔴 THE PAPER CONTAINS NO STATISTICAL ANALYSIS AT ALL, AND USES THE WORD 'SIGNIFICANTLY' FOR ITS OWN COMPARISONS ANYWAY. Measured over the whole body: zero occurrences of a statistics section, of any p-value, of t-test, Student, ANOVA, SEM or a stated n. Error bars are labelled STDV in three captions and panel 6d has none. Yet the Results describe an eightfold increase in cell death as significant, and the transactivation suppression as significant and dose-dependent. The effects in Figure 6 are large — roughly 4% dead cells for cisplatin alone against about 14% for WWOX plus doxycycline plus cisplatin — so the direction is not in doubt; what is absent is any test, and the word asserts one.

entries.proposition: THE INTERACTION MAPPING AND THE TRANSACTIVATION ARMS, INSPECTED AND CONSISTENT. Recorded because an audit that reports only failures is not an audit. Figure 1 shows WWOX co-precipitating with ΔNp63α and not TAp63α across four independent formats; Figure 2 maps the interaction to WW1 — GST-WW1 and GST-WW1+2 pull down ΔNp63α while WW2 and SDR do not — and shows the PY mutant AAxA still binding, which is the paper's own unexpected result; Figure 5 shows dose-dependent suppression of K14 and BPAG-1 reporters by WWOX and a partial rescue by Y33R. All support the text.
